paper_level_summary_zh: 本文在相关工作部分将[23]列为激光麦克风类攻击的一个例子，指出其需要主动发射激光、隐蔽性差、对位置敏感且需要恶意软件安装。属于普通的related work列举，未对目标论文‘Thru-the-wall Eavesdropping on Loudspeakers via RFID by Capturing Sub-mm Level Vibration’进行任何亚毫米级能力或首次开创性评价。

evidences.evidence_quote: Laser-based eavesdroppings [20]–[23] are active methods that require the eavesdropper to direct a laser beam directed at a vibrating object and recover sound from the reflected laser beam.
evidences.evidence_context: Laser-based eavesdroppings [20]–[23] are active methods that require the eavesdropper to direct a laser beam directed at a vibrating object and recover sound from the reflected laser beam. However, it can be easily detected by the victim due to the laser spot.
evidences.reference_entry: S. Sami, S. R. X. Tan, Y. Dai, N. Roy, and J. Han, "Lidarphone: acoustic eavesdropping using a lidar sensor," in Proceedings of the 18th Conference on Embedded Networked Sensor Systems, 2020, pp. 701–702.
evidences.why_this_judgment_zh: 引用论文正文中[23]被列为激光麦克风方法的参考文献，但[23]实际指向的是Lidarphone（激光雷达传感器窃听），并非目标论文‘Thru-the-wall Eavesdropping on Loudspeakers via RFID’。该引用是虚假阳性。 原文证据句引用了其他编号，没有引用目标论文编号。
evidences.copy_ready_zh: 引用文献[23]实际对应的是Lidarphone论文，而非RFID亚毫米振动感知的目标论文，属于错误关联。
